name: Carian Pantheon
note: Hub collective for the indigenous civic deities of Caria attested at the major rural sanctuaries (Labranda, Lagina, Mylasa, Panamara, Sinuri); Laumonier 1958.

name: Zeus Labraundos
note: The double-axe-wielding Zeus of the great sanctuary at Labranda near Mylasa, indigenous Carian storm/war god interpreted as Zeus; epigraphically Zeus Labraundos/Labrayndos, his priest the Hekatomnids' dynastic cult (Mausolus, Idrieus). Laumonier 1958, pp. 37-101.

name: Zeus Osogo (Zenoposeidon)
note: Carian god of Mylasa worshipped as Zeus Osogo / Osogoa, also called Zenoposeidon (Zeus-Poseidon); his temple held a saltwater spring and the trident appeared with the eagle, fusing Zeus and Poseidon. Laumonier 1958, pp. 102-145.

name: Zeus Panamaros (Zeus Stratios)
note: Zeus of the federal sanctuary at Panamara near Stratonikeia, also titled Zeus Stratios ('of the army'); patron of the Panamareia festival and famed epiphany that repelled a siege. Laumonier 1958, pp. 221-343.

name: Hecate of Lagina
note: The great Carian Hecate venerated at the sanctuary of Lagina near Stratonikeia, with her annual Kleidos Pompe (procession of the key) and mysteries; a major civic cult equating the indigenous goddess with Greek Hecate. Laumonier 1958, pp. 344-425.

name: God of Sinuri
note: Indigenous Carian deity (Theos Sinuri) of the rural sanctuary of Sinuri near Mylasa, known from the Hekatomnid-era archive and Carian inscriptions; an autochthonous god retaining his native name rather than a Greek interpretatio. Laumonier 1958, pp. 198-220; Sinuri sanctuary archive.
